name: flask
note: Written from the source at this commit. expected_files are paths relative to the repo root; a retrieved record counts as relevant if its file is in the list. Split alternates dev/test in the order the questions were written, fixed before any results were seen.

questions.question: How does the flask command find the application object in a module?
How are environment variables that start with FLASK_ loaded into the config?
How is the session cookie signed, and how are old secret keys still accepted?
How does the session serializer keep tuples, bytes and datetimes when it stores them as JSON?
What happens when a view returns a tuple instead of a response object?
How does Flask choose which error handler to call for an exception?
Why does adding a route after the app has handled its first request raise an error?
How does a blueprint add its URL prefix and name to the routes it registers?
How does a class-based view send the request to the method named after the HTTP verb?
How are flashed messages stored and read back on the next request?
How does send_from_directory stop a request from reading files outside the directory?
How are dates, decimals and dataclasses turned into JSON in a response?
How can a streaming generator keep using the request after the view has returned?
How are async view functions run?
How can a test change the session before making a request with the test client?
How are templates looked up when blueprints have their own template folders?
Where does the app's logger send messages by default?
What error explains that request.files is empty because the form was not sent as multipart/form-data?
How is the maximum size of a request body set and enforced?
In the tutorial app, how is a page protected so only logged-in users can see it?
